articles.title: Chennai Corporation's first food court delayed, opening pushed to 2027
articles.description: Chennai, Oct 20 (IANS) Residents will have to wait until 2027 to visit the Greater Chennai Corporation’s first food court, with construction of the Rs 4.24-crore facility at Indira Nagar Third Avenue in Adyar progressing well behind its original schedule. Only about 40 per cent of the project has been completed, more than a year after it was announced. Initially scheduled to welcome visitors during Pongal 2026, the food court missed that deadline and a subsequent opening target in August. The Corporation is developing the facility on land occupied by an unused shopping complex belonging to the civic body. A portion of the old complex was demolished to make way for the project, with foundation and structural work beginning earlier this year. The food court will accommodate 30 shops in two sizes. Smaller outlets will measure 110 square feet each, while the larger units will cover 220 square feet. Announced on July 7, 2025, the project was expected to bring food outlets together at a single Corporation-owned location. However, the slow pace of construction has repeatedly pushed back the date on which residents can use the facility. Corporation officials attributed the delay to the 2026 Assembly election and the subsequent change in government. Custom Ad: Multiplex Structural work on the shops is now expected to be completed by December, according to a senior GCC official. Completion of the buildings, however, will not immediately pave the way for opening the food court. The Corporation must also select an operator through a tender process scheduled to begin in January 2027. The civic body has decided to adopt a revenue-sharing arrangement under a public-private partnership model. Instead of directly renting individual shops to restaurant brands, franchises or other food businesses, it will lease the entire facility to a single operator. The proposed arrangement means the selection of that operator will be a key stage in bringing the project into public use after construction. Although officials have indicated when structural work should end and tendering should begin, they have not specified a firm opening date in 2027. For residents awaiting the facility, the revised schedule represents another extension of a project originally promised for Pongal this year. Its opening will now depend on both the completion of the remaining construction and the progress of the tendering process, extending the wait beyond the earlier targets. --IANS aal/dpb

articles.title: Curent Affairs One- Liner: 16th,17th,18th & 19th October 2026
articles.description: National: On 16 October 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) published a draft amendment to the Foods for Infant Nutrition Regulations, 2020, proposing to prohibit added sucrose and fructose in products intended for infants up to six months. The proposal aims to reduce early exposure to added sugars and strengthen age-appropriate nutritional standards. Stakeholders were given 60 days to submit suggestions or objections. For examinations, remember that this is a draft proposal, rather than an already implemented nationwide prohibition. On 16 October 2026, a Spot-bellied Eagle-Owl was photographed in Janakikkad forest, Kozhikode district, Kerala. Scientifically known as Ketupa nipalensis, previously classified as Bubo nipalensis, this large nocturnal bird generally inhabits forested landscapes. Its documentation adds to knowledge of the region’s bird diversity and highlights the conservation importance of remaining forest habitats. On 17 October 2026, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) notified trade-margin rationalisation for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, with revised prices effective from 9 November 2026. The measure caps trade margins at 30%, seeking to reduce excessive mark-ups and improve access to cancer treatment. Prices of affected medicines could fall by up to 70%. NPPA functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. The decision invokes Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013. A report dated 19 October 2026 highlighted the spread of Lantana camara, an invasive shrub introduced into India as an ornamental plant during the nineteenth century. It competes with native vegetation, alters forest undergrowth and can obstruct wildlife movement and natural regeneration. The frequently cited estimate of over 13 million hectares is not a new October 2026 census; similar estimates appeared in earlier research. A wildlife survey conducted from 8–11 October 2026 in Kerala’s Peechi wildlife division recorded 395 species, adding 36 to existing checklists. Organised by the Forest and Wildlife Department with the Travancore Nature History Society, it covered Peechi–Vazhani, Chimmony and Chulannur protected areas. Researchers recorded 165 bird species, 174 butterfly species and 56 dragonfly and damselfly species. The additions comprised eight birds, 22 butterflies and six odonates. These are new records for local checklists, rather than necessarily newly discovered species. On 18 October 2026, Telangana celebrated Saddula Bathukamma, the concluding day of the state’s nine-day floral festival. Women arranged seasonal flowers into tiered structures, sang traditional songs and participated in community celebrations, including events around Hyderabad’s Tank Bund. Bathukamma celebrates nature, cultural identity and women’s participation in community life. The festival is closely associated with Goddess Gauri and Telangana’s seasonal floral diversity. On 15 October 2026, Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced that India’s Ramsar-site total had reached 103, following the designation of Sukhna Wetland in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh. Ramsar designation recognises wetlands of international importance under the convention adopted at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971. The framework promotes wetland conservation and wise use, including protection of ecological characteristics and biodiversity. On 15 October 2026, reporting on a notice directing actor Imran Khan, an American national, to leave India renewed discussion of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 and OCI rights. Overseas Citizen of India status is not Indian citizenship and does not provide unrestricted political rights. Foreign nationals remain subject to immigration conditions and applicable government directions. The reported notice cited Sections 7 and 29. On 15 October 2026, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) recognised ZT Lalrithangi of Mizoram and Priyanka Mahesh Shelke of Maharashtra under its 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development Initiative. Lalrithangi’s recognition highlighted sustainable horticulture and rural entrepreneurship, including strawberry cultivation. The initiative honours women contributing to food systems, community livelihoods and sustainable agricultural development. India’s Agriculture Ministry nominated 20 women for consideration. On 14 October 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved ₹2,009.61 crore as 78 days’ Productivity Linked Bonus for 11,40,770 railway employees. The payment recognises employees’ contribution to railway performance and is intended to encourage productivity. Eligible categories include operational and supporting railway staff covered by the approved scheme. On 14 October 2026, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu inaugurated a 2 MW solar power project with battery storage at Rongtong near Kaza, Spiti Valley. Built at approximately ₹4.42 crore, it incorporates 1 MWh of battery storage to improve electricity reliability in the remote high-altitude region. Its distinction is being Himachal Pradesh’s first solar project equipped with battery energy storage, rather than the state’s first solar project overall. The initiative demonstrates how renewable generation and storage can support difficult Himalayan operating conditions. Reports dated 14 October 2026 outlined a proposed phased introduction of Bharat Stage VII emission standards between April 2029 and April 2035. The framework would tighten vehicle-emission requirements and place greater emphasis on real-world performance and pollution control across vehicle categories. Implementation schedules would vary for passenger and commercial vehicles, while detailed requirements depend on final notifications. Bharat Stage norms regulate vehicle pollution and are broadly developed with reference to European emission frameworks. A report dated 15 October 2026 highlighted research on the return of Asiatic lions to Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat, after an absence described as approximately 144 years. The study assessed Barda’s potential as an additional stronghold beyond the Gir landscape. Establishing viable populations across suitable habitats can reduce risks arising from disease, disasters and concentration in a single landscape. The news concerns research and the lions’ renewed presence; it should not be presented as a formally organised translocation conducted on the reporting date. On 15 October 2026, the Supreme Court upheld a Madras High Court ruling concerning a Hindu convert’s claim to Backward Class Muslim reservation. The Court held that pre-conversion caste or community status cannot automatically establish membership of a different notified backward community after conversion. Eligibility requires the necessary legal and social connection with the claimed community. Scheduled Caste status and OBC/BC eligibility involve different legal provisions. On 12 October 2026, Union Health Minister JP Nadda laid the foundation stone for the ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong, Himachal Pradesh. The centre will study health challenges associated with low oxygen, extreme cold and Himalayan living conditions. Research will benefit both civilian communities and personnel serving at high altitude. Collaboration involving ICMR, Armed Forces Medical Services and AIIMS Bilaspur is envisaged. The foundation ceremony marks the start of infrastructure development, rather than confirmation that the completed facility has begun functioning. On 15 October 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and dedicated five development projects worth approximately ₹3,350 crore in Ladakh through video conferencing. The projects aim to strengthen infrastructure, connectivity and essential services in the Union Territory. Such investments have particular importance in a high-altitude border region where geography and weather complicate service delivery and construction. The total represents several development projects, rather than a single scheme carrying the entire allocation. On 14 October 2026, the Central Government approved India’s accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA). The agreement provides a regional framework for conserving and sustainably managing fishery resources in relevant high-seas areas of the southern Indian Ocean. Participation would strengthen India’s role in fisheries governance and support opportunities for its fishing fleet beyond national waters. The decision follows India’s December 2025 high-seas fisheries guidelines. Accession does not provide unlimited fishing rights; vessels remain subject to applicable conservation, reporting and management measures. On 14 October 2026, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) launched a Silver Refinery Scheme during the national celebration of World Standards Day in New Delhi. The event also featured standards concerning emerging technologies, clean-energy mobility and healthcare, alongside roadmaps for sustainable agriculture and manufacturing. The initiatives seek to strengthen quality assurance, consumer confidence and India’s standardisation infrastructure. On 15 October 2026, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal launched the National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The centre supports data-driven monitoring, trade intelligence and evidence-based policymaking. Its tools facilitate product-wise and market-wise analysis, identification of export opportunities and monitoring of strategic trade matters. During the launch, attention was given to the SCOMET dashboard, covering sensitive dual-use and strategic items. On 16 October 2026, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena announced the creation of Sankoo as the Union Territory’s eighth district, carved out of Kargil. The announcement addressed longstanding demands for closer administration and improved access to public services. Reports also stated that Sankoo would have a separate hill council, with elections to follow. Administrative announcements, operational establishment of district offices and elections to representative institutions are separate stages of implementation. International: Reporting dated 18 October 2026 drew attention to Limoges Town Hall in France after the historic building was damaged during unrest. Opened in 1883, the nineteenth-century structure is associated with neo-Renaissance architecture and was inspired by Paris’s town hall. It serves as a municipal administrative building and is an important part of Limoges’s architectural heritage. The incident raised concerns about protecting public monuments during civil disturbances. On 15 October 2026, REC Limited disclosed receipt of an RBI No Objection Certificate concerning its proposed merger with Power Finance Corporation (PFC). Both institutions are major lenders to India’s power and infrastructure sectors. The proposed combination seeks to consolidate financing capabilities and institutional resources. However, the RBI’s NOC does not mean that the merger has been completed; other statutory requirements, including relevant shareholder and creditor approvals, remain applicable. completion. Banking: Through a notification dated 8 October 2026, reported on 12 October, SEBI introduced a Common Advertisement Code (CAC) for regulated market entities. It permits celebrity endorsements at the brand or entity level, while prohibiting endorsement of specific financial products or services. Covered entities include brokers, depository participants, investment advisers, research analysts, portfolio managers and mutual fund-related entities. The objective is consistent advertising standards and stronger investor protection. On 15 October 2026, Karnataka Bank introduced Nava Dhamaka 2026, comprising nine banking products and service enhancements, at its Bull Temple Road office in Bengaluru. The initiative covers investments, payments, digital banking, customer engagement and lending. Features include enhanced internet and mobile banking, UPI access for eligible NRI customers, CBDC-related functionality, institutional payment collection solutions and startup finance. Managing Director and CEO Raghavendra S Bhat inaugurated the programme. Its theme, Enhancing Banking Experience, emphasises technology-supported banking convenience and broader customer access. On 15 October 2026, HSBC India announced a ₹200 crore philanthropy programme running from 2026 to 2030 to strengthen financial literacy. The programme aims to help communities use formal and digital financial services safely, recognise fraud and make informed financial decisions. Implementation involves partnerships with nonprofit organisations, educational institutions and research bodies The announced amount is a programme commitment, rather than an immediate payment to beneficiaries. Economy: Reports dated 18 October 2026 stated that AdaniConneX’s proposed Visakhapatnam data-centre campuses, developed with Google, would use air-based cooling to limit freshwater consumption. The design avoids water-intensive evaporative cooling systems at the proposed sites. The development highlights the importance of assessing electricity demand, water use and environmental sustainability as India expands artificial-intelligence infrastructure. These are project-design commitments rather than verified operating results from completed campuses. Data released on 15 October 2026 showed India’s net direct tax collections rising 13.2% year-on-year to ₹13.38 lakh crore, up to 14 October in the financial year. Direct taxes principally include corporate income tax and personal income tax, with net collections calculated after refunds. The figures provide an indication of revenue mobilisation and the government’s fiscal position. According to reporting dated 15 October 2026, preliminary RBI data placed India’s August 2026 current account deficit at US$5.2 billion, compared with US$6.1 billion a year earlier. The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to US$26.6 billion, while the services surplus increased to US$16.5 billion. A current account deficit arises when payments relating to goods, services and income exceed corresponding receipts, after transfers are included. On 13 October 2026, ReNew announced a US$100 million financing facility from FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. The 10-year funding, extended to ReNew Solar Power Private Limited, will support renewable-energy projects under construction across the group. The company described it as FMO’s largest single-ticket investment in India’s energy sector. The transaction demonstrates the role of international development finance in India’s clean-energy transition. On 13 October 2026, India notified a protocol amending the India–Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, introducing a Principal Purpose Test (PPT), with the protocol reported as effective from 10 August 2026. The test enables denial of treaty benefits when securing those benefits is one of the principal purposes of an arrangement, subject to the treaty’s provisions. It seeks to address treaty abuse and inappropriate tax avoidance. On 8 October 2026, the World Trade Organization (WTO) raised its forecast for global merchandise trade-volume growth in 2026 to 3.9%, from 1.9% in its March baseline. Strong demand for artificial-intelligence-related goods helped support the revision despite geopolitical and energy-related disruptions. The WTO also projected 4.1% growth for 2027. These figures are forecasts, which remain sensitive to policy changes, conflict and international demand. On 15 October 2026, Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma launched four digital financial-management initiatives at the Chief Minister’s Office in Aizawl: Mizoram Integrated Works Accounts System, e-Sanction, e-Budget and 100% Direct Benefit Transfer. They aim to improve transparency, expenditure monitoring, administrative efficiency and timely benefit delivery. The systems address different parts of public financial management, from budgeting and sanctions to works accounts and beneficiary payments. Reporting dated 16 October 2026 announced financing agreements involving the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Government of Japan and AM Green Ammonia (India) Private Limited for a renewable-powered ammonia project in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh. The project supports industrial decarbonisation by developing ammonia production linked to renewable energy. Green ammonia can serve fertiliser production and emerging low-carbon fuel markets. Sports: On 16 October 2026, Indian para-table-tennis player Bhavina Patel began her Asian Para Games campaign with a 3–0 victory over Kuwait’s Ahad Alrasheedi. Competing in the women’s singles Class 4–5 Group A event at the Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, she won 11–6, 11–3, 11–6. The result represented an opening group-stage victory, rather than a medal-winning final. Bhavina is also known for winning silver at the Tokyo Paralympics. On 18 October 2026, South Korea’s An Se Young won the Denmark Open women’s singles badminton title at SJF Bank Arena, Odense, Denmark. She defeated Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi 21–23, 21–14, 21–18 in the final. The victory was reported as her 47th international singles title, establishing a women’s singles record, and her ninth international title of the season. On 17 October 2026, Manasi Joshi and Thulasimathi Murugesan assured India of a medal in women’s doubles SL3–SU5 para-badminton at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. They defeated China’s Yuemei Liu and Tongtong Li 21–10, 21–17, securing a semifinal place through a top-two group finish. The result assured a medal because both losing semifinalists receive bronze in the event. At that stage, the final medal colour had not been decided. The pair had also won silver at the previous Hangzhou edition. On 19 October 2026, Indian para-archer Sheetal Devi scored 704 points in the women’s compound ranking round at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games, Japan, equalling the world record. The mark matched the record associated with Türkiye’s Öznur Cüre Girdi at the Paris Paralympics. Sheetal’s performance strengthened India’s position in the competition, but a ranking-round record is distinct from winning a medal in an elimination final. Reports dated 17 October 2026 recorded Amruta Pujari’s silver medal in the women’s 72 kg category at the Under-23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas, United States. She lost the gold-medal bout 0–6 to Ukraine’s Iryna Zablotska, having reached the final after defeating China’s Wenjin Qiu in the semifinal. Her achievement contributed to India’s medal tally at the championships. On 18 October 2026, Kenya’s Charles Matata won the men’s elite race at the Delhi Half Marathon, setting a course record of 58 minutes 52 seconds. He improved the previous record, set by Ethiopia’s Amedework Walelegn in 2020, by one second. The event took place in New Delhi, with winners felicitated at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu won the women’s elite race. On 15 October 2026, Indian batter Punam Raut announced her retirement from all formats of international cricket with immediate effect. A top-order batter, she was part of India’s memorable campaign to the 2017 Women’s ODI World Cup final. Her retirement announcement concerns international cricket and should not automatically be interpreted as retirement from every domestic or franchise competition unless separately confirmed. Military Exercise: Reports published on 14 October 2026 highlighted the Assam Regiment’s gold medal at Exercise Cambrian Patrol 2026, held in Wales, United Kingdom. Organised under the British Army’s 160th Welsh Brigade, the annual exercise tests military patrolling, navigation, teamwork, endurance and operational decision-making. Participants include British and international military teams. Often called the Olympics of Military Patrolling, it assesses teams against demanding professional standards. A gold award recognises achievement against the exercise’s assessment criteria; it should not automatically be described as a single overall championship victory over every participating team. Exercise IBSAMAR IX, scheduled from 8–21 October 2026 around Simon’s Town, South Africa, brings together the navies of India, Brazil and South Africa. India deployed the guided-missile stealth frigate INS Tarkash. Hosted by South Africa, the exercise aims to strengthen interoperability, maritime security and professional cooperation through harbour and sea activities. Its theme is Stronger Together Towards a Shared Future in the Maritime Domain. Training includes surface, anti-air and anti-submarine operations, maritime interdiction, search and rescue, and damage control. IBSAMAR began in 2008. Science and Technology: A report published on 16 October 2026 described three new South Indian centipede species: Rhysida quadrispinosa, Rhysida coorgensis and Rhysida neyyarensis. Researchers associated with the Zoological Survey of India’s Western Ghat Regional Centre, Kozhikode, and Malabar Christian College participated in the work. The names refer to distinctive spines, Coorg in Karnataka, and Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala. The findings highlight the Western Ghats’ biodiversity and the importance of taxonomic research. Scientists distinguished the species through anatomical characteristics, rather than simply differences in colour or collection location. As of 19 October 2026, Japan’s Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission was scheduled for launch on 20 October 2026. Led by JAXA, it aims to study Mars’s moons and return surface material from Phobos to Earth. The samples could help determine whether the moons originated as captured asteroids or formed following a major impact involving Mars. The mission involves international cooperation with agencies including NASA, CNES, DLR and ESA.. According to reporting dated 19 October 2026, ISRO’s SpaDeX satellites SDX01 and SDX02 re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on 12 October 2026, in UTC, approximately seven hours apart. Launched on 30 December 2024, the Space Docking Experiment demonstrated technologies for spacecraft rendezvous, docking, separation and power transfer. India’s first successful docking occurred on 16 January 2025, making it the fourth country to demonstrate the capability. Docking technology supports future complex missions, including orbital assembly and servicing. The re-entry dates should be quoted with their stated time standard. On 22 September 2026, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova and Tomáš Jungwirth received the 2026 Europhysics Prize for work establishing altermagnetism as a fundamental class of magnetic order. Awarded by the European Physical Society’s Condensed Matter Division, the recognition highlights research extending the traditional understanding of ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism. Altermagnetic materials combine characteristics relevant to both established classes while exhibiting distinctive electronic properties. Their study could influence spintronics, quantum materials and information technologies. On 6 October 2026, the University of Arizona publicised its leadership of NASA’s PUFFINS mission, with Ramya Anche as principal investigator. The name expands to Polarimetry in the Ultraviolet to Find Features in INterStellar dust. The small satellite will examine how dust alters ultraviolet light from approximately 70 stars, improving understanding of dust properties and its role in star and planet formation. NASA lists a planned 2029 launch under its Astrophysics Pioneers programme. The mission studies interstellar dust; it is not a confirmed life-detection mission. Research reported on 16 October 2026 identified WD J1330+6435, a white dwarf approximately 280 light-years away in Draco, as having an unusual chartreuse-green appearance. Its colour is associated with its atmospheric chemistry and the absorption of particular wavelengths, rather than green being the normal temperature-based colour of stars. A white dwarf is the dense remnant left by a low- or intermediate-mass star after it sheds its outer layers. The finding highlights how atmospheric composition can affect the observed or modelled appearance of stellar remnants. r Reporting dated 16 October 2026 described a demonstration of Tesla’s next-generation Roadster near Waco, Texas, involving a curved ramp, inverted movement and an aerial flip. Elon Musk shared the demonstration, attracting attention to the proposed use of advanced vehicle-control and thrust-assisted technologies. The event generated renewed interest in the long-delayed electric sports car. Demonstrated stunt capability, production specifications, regulatory approval and routine roadworthiness are separate matters. On 14 October 2026, 3M and Discovery Education named Raji Doshi the winner of the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. Her project uses an algae–aragonite alkalinity system intended to address carbon-dioxide-driven ocean acidification. The competition recognises scientific problem-solving by middle-school students in the United States. Ocean acidification occurs when absorbed carbon dioxide changes seawater chemistry, affecting organisms such as corals and shell-forming animals. On 12 October 2026, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) dedicated its Cyclone Warning and Marine Weather Services Decision Support System to the nation. The interactive WebGIS-based platform supports access to cyclone and marine-weather information for preparedness and decision-making. It was introduced during the post-monsoon Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting, chaired by IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra. The platform strengthens communication among forecasters, authorities and users exposed to coastal hazards. On 15 October 2026, Samsung Semiconductor India Research and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) inaugurated a Quantum Research Lab in Bengaluru. The collaboration aims to advance research in quantum technologies through academic and industrial cooperation. Quantum research examines physical behaviour at very small scales and supports emerging approaches to computing, communication, sensing and materials. On 16 October 2026, ISRO announced successful Crew Module–Service Module separation tests for the Gaganyaan programme. Conducted using a specially instrumented setup at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Thiruvananthapuram, the tests examined the sequence required to separate the crew module before atmospheric re-entry. They included the severing of electrical and fluid connections and operation of separation devices. The work validates a critical safety-related system. Defence: During a port visit reported on 16 October 2026, the Indian Navy’s sail-training ship INS Sudarshini called at Salalah, Oman, as part of Lokayan-2026. The voyage combines practical seamanship training with maritime diplomacy and engagement with overseas Indian communities. The ship hosted members of the Indian diaspora, including students and teachers from Indian School Salalah. Such visits strengthen people-to-people links and naval goodwill. A report dated 18 October 2026 highlighted DRDO’s development of armour approximately 20% lighter for future combat vehicles. Reducing armour weight can improve mobility, fuel efficiency and the amount of equipment a vehicle can carry, while protection requirements remain central to design. The development supports indigenous military-materials research and efforts to reduce dependence on imported technologies. The stated percentage concerns the reported comparison with existing armour; it should not be applied automatically to the weight of an entire vehicle. On 13 October 2026, Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL) announced the dispatch of 450 Nagastra-1R loitering munitions to the Indian Army in a single batch. The Nagpur-based company supplied the systems under an emergency-procurement arrangement. Loitering munitions can remain over an area before striking an identified target, combining surveillance and precision-attack functions. The delivery strengthens indigenous short-range strike capabilities and private-sector participation in defence manufacturing. On 15 October 2026, the Ministry of Defence signed contracts valued at approximately ₹4,106 crore for the GSAT-7C communication satellite and Varunastra heavyweight torpedoes. The satellite supports the Indian Air Force’s communication requirements, while the torpedoes strengthen the Indian Navy’s anti-submarine capability. The procurement contributes to modernisation and indigenous defence production. On 16 October 2026, Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan commissioned INS Samarthak at Karwar, Karnataka. Built indigenously by Larsen & Toubro, it is the Indian Navy’s first indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel. The ship supports activities including trials and evaluation of naval weapons, sensors and equipment, contributing to domestic capability development. Its commissioning advances self-reliance in naval construction and provides a platform for specialised maritime tasks. A Delhi Planning Department notification dated 12 October 2026 established the Delhi Institute for Transformation and Innovation (DITI), following a Cabinet decision dated 28 July 2026. DITI is intended to function as an advisory institution supporting evidence-based policymaking, development strategy and institutional reform. Its responsibilities include policy research, impact assessment, stakeholder consultation and assistance with frameworks such as Vision Delhi 2047. . Committees: A proposal reported on 6 October 2026 envisaged restructuring the GST Council’s officers’ committee system. A new Standing Committee of Officers would have 12 state representatives, with Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka proposed as a non-rotating core and other seats subject to rotation. The framework seeks to simplify technical coordination and decision preparation. The available report describes a proposal, so the headline that five states have already received permanent seats is too definite. Reports dated 14 October 2026 stated that the Centre had constituted a committee headed by NITI Aayog member Ramesh Chand to examine sugarcane farmers’ demands, particularly in Karnataka and Maharashtra. The move followed concerns about cane prices, production costs and the economic position of growers and sugar mills. The panel is intended to study issues and recommend responses. Summits and Conference: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was scheduled to represent India at the 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting during a visit to Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on 19–20 October 2026. Hosted by Tajikistan within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation framework, the meeting focuses on regional economic cooperation, trade, connectivity and organisational matters. Bilateral engagements were also expected. KAUMARACON-2026, the third international conference on Kaumarabhritya or Ayurveda paediatrics, was held from 15–17 October 2026 at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi.
